title: Attaining liberation by giving up ego

scenes.headline: Liberation by Giving Up Ego
scenes.say: Chapter Eighteen. Attaining Liberation by Giving Up Ego. The longest chapter, and the last. Here Krishna gathers the whole Gita together.
Arjuna asks one more question: what is the difference between renunciation and sacrifice? Verse two. {verse}

scenes.headline: Don't give up the good work
visual: Service, charity and austerity purify the wise
Do them without attachment to the fruit
Dropping duty from fear is not renunciation
scenes.say: Some say all work should be given up. Krishna disagrees. Acts of service, charity and discipline should never be abandoned, because they purify even the wise. Do them, but without attachment to their fruits. To drop your duty because it is hard, or because you fear discomfort, is not renunciation at all.
Verse eleven. {verse}

scenes.headline: Five causes of every action
scenes.say: Krishna then lists the five causes of every action: the body, the doer, the instruments of the senses, the many life forces, and providence, the unseen fifth. Anyone who thinks the Self alone is the doer does not see clearly.

scenes.headline: Everything in three modes
visual: Each in goodness, passion or ignorance
scenes.say: Then Krishna takes the three modes of nature from Chapter Fourteen and holds them up to everything we do. Knowledge, action and the doer, the intellect and the will: each one can be in goodness, in passion or in ignorance. It is a complete map of the human being.
Even pleasure comes in three kinds. The pleasure of goodness is like poison at first and nectar at the end. And the pleasure of passion is the reverse. Verse thirty-eight. {verse}
And the work we do in the world, done well and offered to God, is itself worship. Verse forty-six. {verse}
Krishna then speaks about karma and free will. Arjuna's own nature, he says, will make him fight, even if he resolves not to. Verse sixty-one. {verse}

scenes.headline: "Do as you wish"
visual: I have told you the most secret knowledge
scenes.say: And then, after seventeen chapters of teaching, Krishna does something remarkable. He does not command. I have given you knowledge more secret than all secrets, he says. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish. The choice remains Arjuna's.
But he has one last word, spoken with love. Verse sixty-five. {verse}
And then the verse many consider the summit of the Gita. Verse sixty-six. {verse}
Krishna asks: has your delusion been destroyed, Arjuna? And Arjuna answers. Verse seventy-three. {verse}

scenes.headline: Sanjaya's joy
scenes.say: Far away, in the palace, Sanjaya finishes his report to the blind king. By the grace of the sage Vyasa, he says, I heard this wonderful dialogue with my own ears. Every time I remember it, I am thrilled, and every time I recall that marvellous form of Krishna, I rejoice again and again.
And the Gita ends with Sanjaya's conviction. Verse seventy-eight. {verse}

scenes.headline: After the Gita
visual: Dharma prevails, at a great cost
scenes.say: Our book ends here. What happens next comes from the Mahabharata. Arjuna picks up his bow. The war lasts eighteen days, and it is terrible. In the end, dharma prevails, and the Pandavas rule with justice, but they grieve for everyone they lost. The Gita never pretends that doing right is painless. It only promises that it is right.

visual: Keep doing service, charity and austerity
Give up attachment to their fruits
scenes.say: Lesson one. True renunciation is releasing attachment to results, not abandoning duty. Service, charity and discipline purify the one who does them, so they must not be dropped. What is given up is the craving for their fruits. Walking away from duty out of delusion or fear is not renunciation.

visual: The body, the doer, the senses
No one is the sole doer of anything
scenes.say: Lesson two. Five causes drive every action, not the Self alone. The body, the doer, the senses, the life forces and providence all play their part. Whoever understands this stops claiming sole credit, or sole blame, and is not bound by what they do.

scenes.headline: Goodness and passion in action
visual: Sees one Reality in all | Sees only separate things
Acts from duty, without ego | Acts from ego and craving
Steady in success and failure | Tossed by joy and sorrow
scenes.say: Lesson three. Knowledge, action and the doer all come in three modes. In goodness, one sees one Reality in all beings, acts from duty without ego, and stays steady in success and failure. In passion, one sees only separate things and acts from ego and craving. In ignorance, one clings to a single thing as if it were everything, and acts carelessly.

Lesson four. Intellect and resolve also come in three modes. An intellect in goodness clearly knows right from wrong, bondage from freedom. In passion, it confuses them. In ignorance, it calls wrong right. And resolve, too, can serve God, serve desire, or serve only sleep, fear and despair.

scenes.headline: Two kinds of pleasure
visual: Poison at first | Nectar at first
Nectar in the end | Poison in the end
scenes.say: Lesson five. The highest pleasure is bitter at first and sweet at the end. The joy of spiritual practice can feel like poison at the start, and becomes nectar. Sense pleasure is nectar at the start, and turns to poison. And the pleasure of laziness and delusion confuses us from beginning to end.

visual: Four kinds of work, by natural qualities
Not by the family one is born into
Your own work, done well, is worship
scenes.say: Lesson six. The division of labour is based on natural ability, not birth. Thinkers, protectors, merchants and workers are defined by their inner qualities and gifts, not by their family. And doing one's own natural work, offered to God, is a path to perfection.

visual: Absorbed in God: the highest devotion
scenes.say: Lesson seven. Attain liberation through duty, discipline and devotion. Purify the intellect, steady the mind, step back from the pull of the senses, let go of likes and dislikes, live simply, control speech and action, and stay absorbed in God. That person reaches the highest devotion, and through it, God himself.

visual: God in the heart sets karma in motion
Our past choices made our present nature
Within that, we choose: do as you wish
scenes.say: Lesson eight. Human will operates within God's law of karma. God, dwelling in every heart, lets each being work out its karma. But that karma was made by our own past choices, and Krishna still says: do as you wish. We are shaped by what we chose, and we are still choosing.

visual: "I shall liberate you. Do not grieve."
scenes.say: Lesson nine. Surrender to God is the ultimate path. Set aside the sense of being the doer and the owner, offer every action with love, and take refuge in God's will. And God makes a promise: I shall free you from all bondage. Do not grieve.

scenes.headline: Wisdom and action, together
visual: The Lord of yoga | The bow of duty
Wisdom and dharma | Courage and action
Together: victory and peace | Together: lasting prosperity
scenes.say: Lesson ten. Both knowledge and devoted action are required for liberation. The Gita ends where Krishna and Arjuna stand together: the wisdom of dharma and the bow of duty. Knowledge alone is not enough, and neither is action alone. Where both are united, there is victory, prosperity and peace.

scenes.headline: Rise, and act with love
visual: Give up the ego, not the work
scenes.say: So, Chapter Eighteen, and the whole Gita. Give up the ego, not the work. Offer every action to God, and take refuge in him. Let knowledge and action walk together, like Krishna and Arjuna in one chariot. Arjuna's confusion is gone. Now he stands up, and so can we. Thank you for watching Shruti.
